Garbage wrapped up their 2026 tour on Saturday (Nov. 14) with a free concert at Mexico City’s Zócalo, paying tribute to a country they have visited for three decades with a nod to its culture. 

The Scottish-American band performed their song “The World Is Not Enough” from the James Bond film of the same name with a mariachi arrangement. They also invited Paulina Villarreal, drummer of the Mexican rock band The Warning , to sing their iconic track “I Think I’m Paranoid.”

Garbage frontwoman Shirley Manson , 60, made history by becoming the first non-hispanic woman to headline the Zócalo, drawing a crowd of 90,000 people, according to official figures. Before her, superstars Rosalía and Shakira had packed Mexico’s most important public square in 2023 and 2026, respectively.

“It’s one of the biggest honors of our entire career [to play at the Zócalo], and the whole band is very excited,” Manson told Billboard Español before taking the stage. “Really, we’re all really emotional, and we’re so proud to be here tonight, and it’s an extraordinary… It’s a culmination of 30 years of coming to Mexico and playing in this amazing city.”

The Scottish-born artist noted that her outfit — featuring a white veil, a floral tricolor headdress and braided hair — paid homage to Mexican culture, particularly the legendary Mexican painter Frida Kahlo, whose life and work have inspired her.

items.title: Chart Rewind: In 1986, Alabama Had ‘The Touch’ at No. 1
items.summary:
When Alabama edged a spot to No. 1 on Billboard ’s Top Country Albums chart dated Nov. 15, 1986, the band demonstrated it was still in touch with country fans’ tastes, delivering the group’s seventh straight non-holiday leader.

Related 

Chart Rewind: In 2006, Carrie Underwood Carved Her Name Into the No. 1 Spot 

Chart Rewind: In 1976, Vern Gosdin Made His Debut ‘On’ Hot Country Songs 

Chart Rewind: In 2011, Scotty McCreery’s Debut Album Made Him a ‘Clear’ Country Favorite 

The album’s title, The Touch , was apropos. The first single from the package was a cover of The Carpenters’ “Touch Me When We’re Dancing,” which ranked No. 4 on the concurrent Hot Country Songs. That single would rise to No. 1 two weeks later, and the follow-up, “‘You’ve Got’ The Touch,” would reach the summit on April 11, 1987, bringing their run of No. 1 country songs to 21, with an exception for holiday singles and collaborations. That consecutive streak remains a record four decades later.

Bred in Fort Payne, Alabama, the quartet featured frontman Randy Owen, guitarist Jeff Cook, bassist Teddy Gentry and drummer Mark Herndon, selling out arenas while combining country and harmony-based rock influences. True to form, The Touch mixed ballads, uptempo country, old-time rock ‘n’ roll and one track with a touch of New Wave sonics, keeping them at the genre’s forefront even as the New Traditionalist movement was taking over.

The Touch ultimately spent 10 weeks in the pole position on Top Country Albums. Alabama brought its next three releases to No. 1, rolling up 10 consecutive Albums…

In the tracking week ending Nov. 12, you seem pretty sad… earned 62,000 equivalent album units in the United States (up 9%) according to Luminate.

Also in the top 10, Lil Baby clocks his eighth top 10-charted effort as FRESH starts at No. 2, while P1Harmony achieves its third top 10-charted set with the No. 4 bow of BLOW UP .

The Billboard 200 chart ranks the most popular albums of the week in the U.S. based on multi-metric consumption as measured in equivalent album units, compiled by Luminate. Units comprise album sales, track equivalent albums (TEA) and streaming equivalent albums (SEA). Each unit equals one album sale, or 10 individual tracks sold from an album, or 2,500 ad-supported or 1,000 paid/subscription on-demand official audio and video streams generated by songs from an album. items.title: Ocean Colour Scene review – no other band of their era can do it like this
items.summary:
Ulster Hall, Belfast
With two sets of fathers and sons now in the group, as they play all of Moseley Shoals on its 30th anniversary, the indie stalwarts have aged into seismic and soulful performers

‘It’s only 30 years ago,” Simon Fowler says of Moseley Shoals. He would seem to mean it, but 30 years makes Ocean Colour Scene’s breakthrough album as old now as Revolver was when they were making it. The band once derided for raiding the 60s are now heritage themselves. They open the album’s anniversary tour on the stage where Led Zeppelin first played Stairway to Heaven, and you can’t help but appreciate the lineage.

They walk on to Green Onions, fresh from the Crown Bar, and open with You’ve Got It Bad, all supreme Motown stomp. Fowler sings with a hand in his pocket and looks taken aback by the welcome. The casualness is a conduit: his voice has aged into something close to peak Joe Cocker, grained at the edges, honey underneath. Lining Your Pockets is more resounding than ever.

items.title: Watch Travis Barker and Cynthia Erivo perform ‘In The Air Tonight’ as Phil Collins tells Rock & Roll Hall Of Fame: “You haven’t heard the last of me”
items.summary:
Phil Collins was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall Of Fame last night (November 14), with Cynthia Erivo and Blink-182 ‘s Travis Barker joining forces for a performance of his classic ‘In The Air Tonight’ – watch below.

The 75-year-old singer and drummer was honoured at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, becoming a two-time inductee after previously being recognised as a member of Genesis in 2010.

Barker delivered the induction speech, paying tribute to Collins’ influential drumming and his extraordinary success as both a member of Genesis and a solo artist.

“I remember hearing the drums for the first time and being blown away,” he said of ‘In The Air Tonight’. “That sound changed everything.”

He went on to describe the song’s famous drum break as “arguably the most badass drum fill of all time”, before thanking Collins for inspiring generations of musicians.

Following the induction, Erivo delivered a powerful, stripped-back rendition of the 1981 single, with Barker behind the kit to recreate the iconic drum part.

Watch the performance below:

Collins, who attended the ceremony alongside his daughter, Emily In Paris star Lily Collins , was visibly emotional as he received a standing ovation.

The musician, who has experienced a series of serious health problems in recent years, walked to the stage using two canes.

“I’m really not as bad as it looks,” he joked, assuring the audience that his health had improved.

Reflecting on his career, Collins said: “I grew up just wanting to play the drums. Everything else has been a really happy accident.”

He also thanked his…
items.t: Watch Travis Barker and Cynthia Erivo perform ‘In The Air Tonight’ as Phil Collins tells Rock & Roll Hall Of Fame: “You haven’t heard the last of me”

The legendary producer was honoured with the Musical Excellence Award at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, with Neil Young delivering his induction speech.

To celebrate the occasion, the Chili Peppers took to the stage to perform their 1991 hit ‘Give It Away’, taken from the Rubin-produced album ‘Blood Sugar Sex Magik’.

However, all four members of the band – Anthony Kiedis , Flea , John Frusciante and Chad Smith – appeared wearing long grey wigs, bushy fake beards and sunglasses to resemble the producer’s distinctive appearance.

Watch the performance below:

“You can’t kill rock and roll,” he declared. “Thank you.”

Young, who has known Rubin for decades, paid tribute to the producer’s ability to create an environment in which artists can focus entirely on their music.

“The music is all that’s allowed in,” he said, praising the care Rubin takes over the musicians he works with.

Oasis were inducted into the Rock And Roll Hall Of Fame last night (November 14), although none of the band’s members attended the ceremony in Los Angeles.

READ MORE: Oasis live in Cardiff: a supersonic reunion for a new generation 

The Manchester band were honoured at the Peacock Theater, where Better Call Saul star Bob Odenkirk delivered an enthusiastic induction speech, before country singer Stephen Wilson Jr. performed a solo acoustic version of their 1995 hit ‘Wonderwall’.

Addressing the band’s absence, Odenkirk joked: “Anybody surprised they didn’t show up? It would’ve been out of character if they had. I would have been worried.”

The actor went on to reflect on seeing Oasis live twice, beginning with a concert at Los Angeles’ Universal Amphitheater in 1998, which he recalled being underwhelming because the band appeared not to want to be there.

His second experience was considerably more positive, however, as he attended one of their 2025 reunion shows at New Jersey’s MetLife Stadium, which he described as “one of the best nights of my life”.

Oasis being inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall Of Fame yesterday by Bob Odenkirk. pic.twitter.com/07Z2l1xXMm 

— Latest Oasis News (@scyhodotcom) November 15, 2026 

full oasis induction video from the ceremony tonight pic.twitter.com/2RZ1ZeNi9H 

— meg starr ᯓ★ (@tlktnight) November 15, 2026 

Odenkirk also playfully described the band’s songs as “delicate compositions embroidered with inscrutably complex melodies”, before laughing and admitting: “I’m kidding! Fucking bangers!”

He explained that he had…
items.t: Oasis skip Rock & Roll Hall Of Fame induction as Bob Odenkirk hails them “a dose of Viagra for the ego” and Stephen Wilson Jr. covers ‘Wonderwall’

The hugely anticipated game arrives on Thursday (November 19), alongside an official 34-track soundtrack album created by developers Rockstar Games and Atlantic Records.

While only ten tracks had previously been revealed, the complete running order has now emerged after a record store employee reportedly sold a vinyl copy ahead of schedule, with photographs of the album’s sleeve circulating on social media.

Among the new additions are Del Rey’s ‘Crazy For You’, Lipa’s ‘Go Easy’ and Larsson’s ‘Fast Emotion’, alongside ‘Power Trip’ by BLACKPINK ‘s Jennie , ‘Sweet Like Candy’ by Camila Cabello and ‘TRDWFE’ by Rina Sawayama .

The singer has also been confirmed as one of the game’s celebrity radio station hosts , presenting Back Country Radio alongside her husband Jeremy Dufrene and Morgan Wallen.

Hook, who played bass in both bands, was the only Joy Division/New Order member to attend the ceremony, and later delivered an acceptance speech on their behalf.

items.title: Paris Paloma review – arena-scale alt-pop drama from a singer on her way to bigger things
items.summary:
Bristol Beacon
The UK artist combines feminist fury with accessible melodies and a dramatic flair that sees her alternately pogoing and seeking out the wind machines at the prow of the stage

People are dancing to a song they don’t know, with flower garlands in their hair and their arms around their friends. This reaction to Fairy Dance, an unreleased track written about the community that has sprung up around her music, says a lot about the moment Paris Paloma finds herself in, and tonight’s show feels for all the world like a stepping stone to bigger things.

Throughout, Paloma leans in to the built-in drama of songs from her second album, The Fatal Flaw, which pairs ornate folk arrangements with the sort of arena-sized alt-pop production favoured by Florence + the Machine. With a sculpture inspired by surrealist Ithell Colquhoun’s Tree of Veins dominating the stage, she falls to her knees to deliver high notes and seeks out wind machines at the prow of the stage, her flowing crimson dress buffeted as if on a wintry moor.

items.title: Tout selling £1million of U2 tickets has raised questions about clampdown on bot use for bulk-buying
items.summary:
A ticket tout has advertised more than £1million worth of tickets for U2 ‘s upcoming London shows, raising fresh questions about the use of automated bots to bulk-buy tickets and sell them on at inflated prices.

READ MORE: As live music returns, let’s build back fairer – by wiping out unscrupulous touts 

The Irish band’s four nights at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in June 2027, part of their ‘The Greatest Show On Earth’ world tour , sold out shortly after tickets went on sale last week.

However, a new investigation by The Guardian has revealed that one seller listed more than 2,000 tickets for the concerts on resale site StubHub, despite strict limits on the number that any individual buyer can purchase.

The seller, identified as Vladyslav Skrypka and claiming to be based in Harlow, Essex, advertised over 1,800 tickets for one night alone, some at more than four times their original price. If all of the tickets were sold at their advertised prices, they would generate more than £1million in sales.

The findings have raised concerns about how such large quantities of tickets can be obtained, given that the use of automated software to bypass ticket-buying limits has been outlawed in the UK since 2018 .

Adam Webb of the music industry campaign group FanFair Alliance suggested that the listings could indicate either the use of bots or ‘speculative selling’ – where touts advertise tickets they do not yet possess, hoping to acquire them after a buyer has paid.

View this post on Instagram 

Webb questioned whether StubHub had verified the seller’s tickets, asking: “Have they…
items.t: Tout selling £1million of U2 tickets has raised questions about clampdown on bot use for bulk-buying

items.title: Philippines crowned first Eurovision Asia winners as Carmelle triumphs with ‘Sobra-Sobra’
items.summary:
The Philippines has been crowned the first-ever winner of Eurovision Asia, with 19-year-old singer Carmelle taking victory with her song ‘Sobra-Sobra’ – watch her performance below.

The long-awaited spin-off of Eurovision held its inaugural final at the One Bangkok Forum in Thailand yesterday (November 14), with 11 countries competing for the title.

Carmelle, whose full name is Carmelle Collado, finished with 211 points, receiving 93 from the national juries and 118 from the public vote. She topped both categories to finish 41 points ahead of the host country’s representatives, MANG x DAOU, whose song ‘Aroma’ received 170 points.

Vietnam’s Tóc Tiên finished third with ‘EM TIÊN’ on 164 points, while Malaysia and Laos completed the top five.

Carmelle’s winning song ‘Sobra-Sobra’, meaning ‘Too Much’, is a women’s empowerment anthem that combines dance-pop and rap with traditional Filipino instruments, including the kubing and kulintang.

Watch the winning performance below:

Speaking after her victory, Carmelle described the song as “a tribute to all Filipino women”.

“I made history, since this was the first time,” she told the Associated Press. “It’s such a big responsibility for me, because this one is a global stage, so thank you everybody who voted for me.”

The singer, who grew up in the Bicol region of the Philippines, previously found success on televised singing competitions, finishing as runner-up on The Voice Kids and winning Tawag ng Tanghalan . She also appeared on Pinoy Big Brother .

View this post on Instagram 

The contest brought together performers from…

items.title: ‘Connections’ answers and hints for today, November 15

Out of the many daily puzzles available online, the New York Times’ Connections game is one of the trickiest. For those playing for the first time, the goal of Connections is to divide a block of 16 words into four common themes. Some of these – for example, grouping four types of fish – can be very straightforward, while others can be far more abstract. If you’ve found yourself stumped by the latter, we’ve put together Connections answers and hints for today (November 15) below .

READ MORE: Globle answer today – here’s the answer and hints for November 15 

If you already know how to play Connections, you can skip this paragraph to jump straight into today’s solution. But if this is your first time attempting the New York Times’ puzzle (or you just need a refresher), we suggest thinking outside of the box for your answers.

Some groups are deliberately deceptive – using a previous day’s puzzle as an example, you may think ‘Heart’, ‘Cell’, ‘Body’ and ‘Nucleus’ are all connected through biology. But you’d be wrong, as ‘Heart’ and ‘Nucleus’ were actually two of four “Nexus” words on the day we’ve used as an example. Think beyond what a word means literally, try to see subtle patterns, and your luck with Connections will improve drastically. That being said, some days are still fiendishly difficult – and if you’re still stuck, check below for the Connections answer for today.

items.title: James Blunt: ‘Do I have a nickname? Yes, it rhymes with blunt’
items.summary:
The singer on his love for Ibiza, the weirdest thing he’s done in the name of romance, and being signed up for Celebrity Traitors against his will

You were a punching bag for such a long time after You’re Beautiful became a massive hit but your consistent good humour is deeply admirable. Does it ever get tiring?

It was a surprise, at the beginning. I was just a little guy with a dream. And when you achieve your dream, you think people would be happy for you. For them not to be happy for you but angry with you, for your song, seems irrational, an overreaction. It is interesting how people generally want to tear people down for achieving their little dreams. But I’d had a real proper job before that [as a captain in the British army]. My friends might have been on operations in Afghanistan or Iraq, so if I were to complain to them at the time saying, “Oh, the Guardian said something really horrid about me and gave me three stars for my album” – they would be able to talk about who had lost their lives or limbs that day, and that put it all in perspective. And perspective is everything.

Continue reading...
items.t: James Blunt: ‘Do I have a nickname? Yes, it rhymes with blunt’

items.title: ‘Would you breastfeed your own father?’ The goofy, spiky world of art-pop duo Charlotte Adigéry and Bolis Pupul
items.summary:
After wittily blending pop and politics on their debut, the Belgians are now processing their personal lives. We join them for a mindbending tour of their home city of Ghent

Boris Kor Tom Zeebroek is staring up at a grey gothic building in the centre of Ghent, squinting through the late September sun that is covering his home town in a cloak of unseasonal warmth.

Zeebroek is encouraging his bandmate Charlotte Adigéry and I to crane our necks towards the Mammelokker, an 18th-century Flemish relief on the top of the building. It’s a gruesome bit of stone, which sits above the town square and depicts a daughter suckling her own father. The pair are taking me on a tour of their medieval home town, and this disturbing architectural decoration is part of our itinerary.

items.title: ‘Young, Black and female in Brixton is hard’: ​from football to Top Boy and wordplay, the inspiring journey of UK rapper Cristale
items.summary:
Crystal Palace FC or Oxbridge beckoned, but the multitalented MC kept forging her way towards music. She explains how she poured every aspect of herself into her debut mixtape

Two weeks before we meet, UK rapper Cristale was scrambling down a cliff face to a secluded black pebbled beach in Dover, racing an incoming tide with fewer than 90 minutes to shoot the video for her single I’m Okay With Being Lonely. She’d never hiked before in her life. “I was wearing head-to-toe Stone Island, no hiking gear, full face of makeup, edges laid and Mum was doing my touch-ups on a rusty ladder,” she laughs.

As we sit in her publicist’s central London office, her hair half-braided and half-flowing past a black puffer coat, she says the rush of adrenaline hasn’t fully faded. In fact she seems to thrive on regular bumps of it: beyond her relentlessly articulate and energetic rap flow – put to work on tracks that span drill, introspective R&B and beyond – she has ably hopped between football, art, acting in Netflix projects and more.

items.title: ‘My partners would all tell you I was a nut job’: Jane Wiedlin on the Go-Go’s, fame and the freedom of sex dungeons
items.summary:
As she releases a brutally honest memoir, the new wave icon opens up about industry sexism, living with bipolar disorder and becoming ‘the world’s first atheist ordained minister’

The first thing Jane Wiedlin tells me before our interview even begins is that, an hour or so earlier, she downed two beers. “It keeps me cheerful,” she says with a laugh. The disclosure dovetails with the reason we’re doing the interview in the first place, which is to unpack her new memoir, a tome that deserves a truth-in-advertising award for its title alone: TMI (as in “too much information”). “I’ve always been TMI!” Wiedlin proudly announces. “I’m the one who always wanted to expose the truth. This book is my first opportunity to do so.”

A portion of that truth has to do with the band she helped form in the late 70s, the Go-Go’s. The five-piece are not only the first all-female band who play their own instruments and write their own material to earn a No 1 album in the US but, astonishingly, are the only such group to hold that distinction nearly 45 years later. The group’s power-pop music, heard in zippy hits like Our Lips Are Sealed and Vacation, led to their induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2021, inspired a Broadway play and influenced modern female artists all the way from Olivia Rodrigo to Wet Leg.

items.t: ‘My partners would all tell you I was a nut job’: Jane Wiedlin on the Go-Go’s, fame and the freedom of sex dungeons
